title: Fermionic pairs, from the surface to the bulk
summary: Fermion pairing underlies collective quantum phenomena across widely different forms of matter. In extended systems such as ultracold Fermi gases, pairing is commonly understood through the BCS--BEC crossover, where the pair size evolves from large, overlapping Cooper pairs to tightly bound dimers. In finite systems such as atomic nuclei, superconducting grains and quantum dots, however, the same pairing tendency competes with confinement, shell filling and spatial inhomogeneity, making the microscopic structure of pairs much harder to access.
